subject: Follow-up: socket/connection limits, QPS & streaming requirements
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@morphalabs.com>

Cc: Aisha Khalid <aisha.k@morphalabs.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo – connection model & burst profile

Sean / team, thanks for the demo earlier today — super helpful. Per our conversation, here are the concrete requirements and a brief traffic profile we promised to share: 

- Primary workload: real-time document enrichment for our web product (HTML -> structured JSON).
- Latency SLO: p95 generation end-to-end <= 300 ms for short requests (<=512 tokens); p95 <= 800 ms for multi-chunk streams.
- Expected steady-state: 6,000 completed requests per minute during business hours (~100 rps sustained).
- Peak bursts: up to 5,000 concurrent open requests during marketing events (bursts lasting 3–8 minutes).
- Most requests are streaming (we prefer gRPC/chunked streaming) to render partial tokens quickly.
- Connection behavior: clients are behind a small fleet of edge proxies (approx. 60 source IPs), each maintains persistent HTTP/2 connections where possible.

Attached: morpho-throughput-profile.csv — has sample minute-level traces and a short summary tab.

Open questions for Redwood we discussed and want in writing:
1) What are default per-key connection/streaming limits (concurrent streams, HTTP/2 multiplexing behavior)?
2) How do Redwood rate limits interact with connection pool settings (are there separate "concurrency slots" vs "QPS" limits)?
3) If we need higher concurrency for bursts, what's the fastest path to getting higher limits (config change, Dedicated plan, or signed SLA)?

We'd like a short follow-up summary and proposed next steps by EOD tomorrow if possible. Thanks — Liam

--

Liam / Aisha — great speaking earlier. Quick summary and our working assumptions; I'll loop in SRE for the nitty-gritty.

Summary of what we heard (agree if this matches):
- Steady 100 rps with short bursts to 5k concurrent streaming requests.
- Primary path will be streaming (HTTP/2 or gRPC preferred).
- Need p95 <= 300 ms for short calls; longer for multi-chunk streams.

Immediate answers to your numbered questions: 
1) Defaults: hosted API keys have two quota dimensions: (a) request rate (requests per second / minute) and (b) concurrency slots (open in-flight requests). Default hosted-tier: 400 reqs/s and 200 concurrent slots per org. These are intentionally conservative to protect shared pools.
2) Interaction: concurrency slots govern simultaneous in-flight requests (streams). QPS/rate limits are enforced separately; you can hit one without the other. For streaming, each open stream consumes a concurrency slot until it’s closed; token rates also apply to streaming throughput.
3) Path to higher limits: for predictable burst capacity at your scale we recommend Redwood Dedicated or an Enterprise SLA on Hosted. We can also grant temporary quota increases for pilots (requires a short intake and commitment to a traffic profile).

Quick ask from our side: can you confirm whether your edge proxies will reuse long-lived HTTP/2 connections (multiplex many streams) or will they spawn many short-lived TCP/TLS connections? That changes connection pool sizing. Also, please share one-minute sample traces for a marketing-burst window (the CSV you attached is exactly the right format).

Next steps I propose: 
- I'll coordinate a call with our SRE (Rishi) tomorrow to validate connection-model assumptions and list exact quota changes required for a pilot.
- We’ll produce an initial quote for a temporary quota increase + Dedicated uplift options and attach an example ratecard.

Attaching a high-level quote doc for reference (redwood-ratecard-quote.pdf). Will follow up with engineering notes.

Best,

Subject: Re: Post-demo – connection model & burst profile (SRE notes)

Thanks for the detail, Liam. A few technical notes and options from infra: 

Short answers first:
- Hosted defaults Sean quoted are correct for our standard orgs (400 rps, 200 concurrency slots).
- For streaming, if clients multiplex many logical streams over a small set of persistent HTTP/2 connections we can support a lot more logical streams without raising TCP connection counts, but we still count each in-flight logical stream against the concurrency quota.
- We do not have per-source-IP hard caps for Hosted, but excessive TLS handshakes (lots of short-lived conns) will add CPU overhead and can trigger protective throttles if it looks like a DDOS pattern.

Options to handle Morphos bursts: 
1) Connection multiplexing (recommended): instruct edge proxies to reuse 8–32 persistent HTTP/2 connections per proxy and multiplex streams. This minimizes TLS churn and keeps TCP/TLS footprint low. Each multiplexed stream still consumes a concurrency slot.
2) Temporary quota bump (pilot): we can provision a 4x concurrency bump for a 30-day pilot (requires intake + basic PO). That would give you 800 concurrency slots on Hosted. Good for moderate bursts but not 5k concurrency peak.
3) Dedicated capacity: best long-term for predictable huge bursts. Dedicated GPU pools and a customer-specific ingress layer let us guarantee thousands of concurrent streams and custom connection-pool tuning; comes with committed monthly minimums.
4) Backpressure & progressive-fallback: suggest using progressive partial responses (streaming of partial tokens) and server-side caching for common prefixes to reduce token throughput under load.

Sizing guidance based on your CSV: your ~100 rps steady + marketing spikes to 5k concurrent suggests two viable paths: a short pilot with streaming multiplex + temporary 4x concurrency bump to evaluate behavior, or go straight to Dedicated if you want strong SLA during marketing events.

Action items we need from Morpho to scope a pilot: 
- Confirm edge behavior (how many persistent connections per proxy).
- Provide one representative burst minute trace with exact open-stream counts. (CSV OK.)
- Expected token rates per request (median token out + token in).

Attaching a simple connection model diagram for our internal sizing (conn-model.png). I'll also draft a quote for the temporary bump to 800 slots and an estimated Dedicated starting configuration.

-Rishi

2) If pilot shows repeated headroom problems during bursts, we’ll recommend moving to Dedicated with the following target: 5k concurrent stream capacity, custom autoscale policy for marketing windows, and a modest committed minimum. We'll include pricing options in the Dedicated quote.
